title: Iff-split of IMO 1964 P1(a): n % 3 = 0 iff 2^n = 1 (mod 7)
intent: Split the iff n ∈ solution_set ↔ 2^n ≡ 1 [MOD 7] into its two directions with constructor. The forward direction builds the congruence from a divisibility witness of n % 3 = 0; the reverse direction refutes the non-zero residues of n % 3 with a further case split.

children.name: forward
children.statement: n ∈ solution_set → 2^n ≡ 1 [MOD 7] (first goal created by constructor)
children.closed_by: obtain ⟨m, hm⟩ := Nat.dvd_of_mod_eq_zero hn; change 2^n % 7 = 1; rw [hm, Nat.pow_mul, Nat.pow_mod]; norm_num

children.name: reverse
children.statement: 2^n ≡ 1 [MOD 7] → n ∈ solution_set (second goal created by constructor)
children.closed_by: change n % 3 = 0; change 2^n % 7 = 1 at hn; rw [(Nat.div_add_mod' n 3).symm, pow_add, pow_mul', Nat.mul_mod, Nat.pow_mod] at hn; mod_cases H : n % 3; exact H / rw [H] at hn; norm_num at hn / rw [H] at hn; norm_num at hn

applicability.goal_shape: A goal of the form P ↔ Q (the ↔ type). Here n ∈ solution_set ↔ 2^n ≡ 1 [MOD 7], which unfolds to n % 3 = 0 ↔ 2^n % 7 = 1.
applicability.use_when: the two directions want genuinely different arguments — a construction (forward: a divisibility witness from n % 3 = 0) versus a refutation by cases (reverse: mod_cases on n % 3) — and each closes without reference to the other.
applicability.avoid_when: one direction is definitional or follows by symmetry; the two directions share the same rewriting (a single rw/calc chain proves both); or the equivalence is definitional and rfl suffices.

claims.claim: constructor (line 33) turns the ↔ goal into exactly two subgoals, and both close: the forward direction in lines 34-38 and the reverse in lines 39-47, with no auxiliary lemma stated between them.

claims.claim: The problem's docstring asks '(a) Find all natural numbers n for which 2ⁿ - 1 is divisible by 7', and the formalisation answers it as the iff n ∈ solution_set ↔ 2^n ≡ 1 [MOD 7] with solution_set := { n | n % 3 = 0 }; the iff is the problem statement, not an internal helper.

The reverse direction embeds a second decomposition: mod_cases H : n % 3 (line 44) splits into three residues; residue 0 closes by exact H, and residues 1 and 2 close by rewriting the hypothesis to a false numeral equality and norm_num (lines 45-47).
The same move — state a problem as P ↔ x ∈ solution_set and split it with constructor — appears in Compfiles/Usa1973P4.lean lines 29-33.

metrics.how_counted: parent = lines 32-47 of the copied file; forward = lines 34-38, reverse = lines 39-47; children = the two goals created by constructor

consequences: constructor on an iff creates exactly two obligations (forward and reverse implication), each to be closed on its own; shared structure between the directions is proved twice. Here the reverse direction is not self-contained: it needs a further case split mod_cases H : n % 3, so the two children differ in difficulty (5 vs 9 lines). Failure mode: splitting an iff whose two directions are the same argument in mirror image doubles the proof instead of shortening it.
